name: Simeon
role: Old man who held the infant Jesus in the temple
whenBasis: Jesus' birth, before Herod's death (4 BC as Schürer reckons it, 1 BC as Steinmann does) and perhaps up to two years before it (Matthew 2:16). See the card on dating Herod's death.
summary: A righteous and devout man in Jerusalem, waiting for the consolation of Israel, to whom the Holy Spirit had revealed that he would not die before he had seen the Lord's Christ. Moved by the Spirit, he came into the temple as Joseph and Mary brought Jesus, took him in his arms and blessed God: now let Your servant depart in peace, for my eyes have seen Your salvation, a light for revelation to the Gentiles.
body: He tells Mary that the child is appointed for the rise and fall of many in Israel, a sign that will be spoken against, “and a sword will pierce your soul as well.”

moments.text: Waiting for the consolation of Israel
Not to die before seeing the Christ
Takes the child in his arms
A sword will pierce your soul

later.text: His song, the Nunc Dimittis from its Latin opening, is sung at Compline and at Anglican Evening Prayer.

sources.title: Book of Common Prayer (1662), Evening Prayer
Liturgy of the Hours, Night Prayer
